question: What is the primary purpose of a nursing audit?

options.A: Evaluating nursing care against set standards
options.B: Calculating monthly salaries for ward staff
options.C: Ordering new medical supplies for the ward
options.D: Punishing nurses who make charting errors

explanation: A nursing audit is designed to assess the quality of care provided by comparing it to established professional benchmarks. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is a nursing audit considered a system check rather than a personal attack?

options.A: It is conducted anonymously by patients after discharge
options.B: It focuses on fixing overall practice gaps rather than blaming individuals
options.C: It only looks at doctors' notes and ignores nursing duties
options.D: It replaces the need for annual performance appraisals

explanation: Audits look at systemic patterns in documentation and care delivery to improve institutional quality rather than penalizing single staff members. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which objective is a direct benefit of conducting regular nursing audits?

options.A: Lowering the market price of pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Improving the overall quality of patient care
options.C: Reducing the duration of basic nursing training
options.D: Increasing the number of hospital admission beds

explanation: The main driver of quality assurance activities is to elevate patient care standards through continuous evaluation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: How do nursing audits support professional growth among clinical staff?

options.A: By determining which nurses deserve salary deductions
options.B: By eliminating the need for licensing examinations
options.C: By providing constructive feedback to guide further training needs
options.D: By automatically granting promotions to senior ward managers

explanation: Audit results highlight specific knowledge or practice gaps, showing educators where extra training is required. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: A nursing audit that takes place after a patient has been discharged is called what?
explanation: Reviewing completed records after a patient leaves the facility is classified as a retrospective audit. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: A nurse manager wants to catch and correct charting errors while the patient is still admitted on the ward. Which audit type should be used?
explanation: Concurrent audits happen in real-time during admission, enabling immediate correction of active care and documentation flaws. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first step in conducting a nursing audit?

options.A: Writing the final report for the medical director
options.B: Punishing staff members with poor records
options.C: Buying new computer software for the ward
options.D: Selecting the topic or aspect of care to evaluate

explanation: Every audit begins by choosing a specific clinical focus or standard to investigate. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is a re-audit performed after implementing corrective actions?

options.A: To fulfill a legal requirement for government tax purposes
options.B: To check if the changes made actually resolved the initial problem
options.C: To justify increasing the hospital fees for patients
options.D: To decide which nurses need to repeat their nursing school exams

explanation: A follow-up or re-audit measures whether interventions successfully improved care quality. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the common audit rule regarding undocumented nursing care?

options.A: Unwritten care is assumed to be perfect
options.B: Missing notes can be filled in after retirement
options.C: If it is not documented, it was not done
options.D: Verbal confirmation from the nurse is enough

explanation: In legal and audit contexts, unrecorded care holds no proof of execution. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why do auditors sometimes use direct observation alongside chart reviews?

options.A: To replace the need for physical patient case notes
options.B: To speed up the discharge process for stable patients
options.C: To find reasons to query junior nurses on duty
options.D: To check if actual bedside practice matches written records

explanation: Observing care firsthand ensures that documentation reflects true clinical actions rather than mere paperwork compliance. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: When does an audit identify a clinical performance gap?

options.A: When actual practice falls below the expected standard
options.B: When the hospital runs out of patient admission beds
options.C: When patient visiting hours are extended by management
options.D: When senior doctors refuse to sign the ward register

explanation: A gap represents the shortfall between established quality benchmarks and actual recorded nursing practice. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is finding the root cause of an audit gap important?

options.A: It lowers the cost of buying new hospital equipment
options.B: It helps design the right solution for the underlying problem
options.C: It stops the need for future ward meetings and reports
options.D: It gives management a reason to dismiss lazy staff members

explanation: Understanding why a failure happens ensures that corrective interventions target the true source rather than just treating symptoms. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h6)

question: What should happen immediately after identifying gaps in a nursing audit?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the year to take any action
options.B: Suspending all nursing shift duties on the affected ward
options.C: Hiding the report from the hospital quality committee
options.D: Implementing corrective measures to address root causes

explanation: The entire purpose of finding audit gaps is to correct them and elevate care quality through active intervention. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: An audit reveals that nurses fail to chart pain assessments because paper forms are confusing. What is the best corrective action?

options.A: Issuing stern warning letters to all nurses on the ward
options.B: Demanding that patients fill out their own pain charts
options.C: Redesigning the chart template to be clearer and simpler
options.D: Stopping all pain assessments until further notice

explanation: Addressing a structural design flaw in documentation tools directly resolves the root cause of the compliance gap. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to nursing audits in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully digitalized electronic records
options.B: Fear of victimization and resistance to change among staff
options.C: Reliance on paper-based records that get misplaced easily
options.D: Severe staff shortages and heavy patient workloads

explanation: Most local facilities still struggle with paper records rather than having an excess of advanced electronic systems. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)

question: Why does severe staff shortage negatively affect the nursing audit process?

options.A: Nurses have little time for detailed documentation and review
options.B: It prevents doctors from writing prescription orders
options.C: It stops nursing students from attending lectures
options.D: It forces hospitals to close down all outpatient clinics

explanation: Overworked nurses stretched across high patient volumes often prioritize immediate physical care over meticulous documentation and audit participation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h8)
